subject: english
label: 英語面接 定番フレーズ
blurb: 自己紹介・強み・志望動機から逆質問・締めまで、面接で言いたい70文
audience: 転職・外資・社内英語面接、留学面接を控えた人

genres.wi-clarify: 聞き返し・間をつなぐ

words.answer: Thank you for this opportunity.
accept: Thank you for the opportunity.
Thank you for giving me this opportunity.
Thank you for this opportunity today.
words.q: 本日はこのような機会をいただき、ありがとうございます。
words.explain: 冒頭は短く一言で。opportunity は可算なので this／the を付ける。Thank you for today だけでは物足りない
words.say: Thank you for this opportunity.

words.answer: I have five years of experience in sales.
accept: I have five years' experience in sales.
I have five years of sales experience.
I have five years' sales experience.
words.q: 私には営業の経験が5年あります。（experience を使って）
words.explain: have experience in ＋分野。experience は不可算なので experiences にしない。年数は five years of の形
words.say: I have five years of experience in sales.

words.answer: I currently work for an IT company.
accept: I'm currently working for an IT company.
I am currently working for an IT company.
Currently, I work for an IT company.
I work for an IT company now.
words.q: 私は現在、IT企業に勤めています。（work for を使って）
words.explain: 会社に勤めるは work for／at。work in は業界や部署（work in IT）。an IT の冠詞は発音が母音なので an
words.say: I currently work for an IT company.

words.answer: I'm in charge of customer support.
accept: I am in charge of customer support.
words.q: 私はカスタマーサポートを担当しています。（in charge を使って）
words.explain: in charge of は責任者に近い響き。単なる担当なら I handle ／ I work in も可。charge に the は付けない
words.say: I'm in charge of customer support.

words.answer: I majored in economics at university.
accept: I majored in economics in college.
I majored in economics at college.
I majored in economics in university.
I majored in economics.
words.q: 大学では経済学を専攻しました。（major を使って）
words.explain: major in ＋分野。studied だけだと専攻か履修か曖昧。university は無冠詞でよい。学部名は小文字
words.say: I majored in economics at university.

words.answer: Let me briefly introduce myself.
accept: Let me introduce myself briefly.
Allow me to briefly introduce myself.
I'd like to briefly introduce myself.
words.q: 簡単に自己紹介させてください。
words.explain: Let me ＋動詞の原形。「自己紹介」は introduce myself。self-introduction は名詞としては通じるが会話では不自然
words.say: Let me briefly introduce myself.

words.answer: I specialize in digital marketing.
accept: I specialise in digital marketing.
words.q: 私の専門はデジタルマーケティングです。（specialize を使って）
words.explain: specialize in ＋分野。My specialty is も可だが料理の得意メニューにも聞こえる。specialize の後は in
words.say: I specialize in digital marketing.

words.answer: Before that, I worked as a software engineer.
accept: Before that, I was a software engineer.
Prior to that, I worked as a software engineer.
Before that, I was working as a software engineer.
words.q: その前は、ソフトウェアエンジニアとして働いていました。
words.explain: work as ＋職種（冠詞 a を忘れない）。時系列は Before that／After that でつなぐと聞き手が追いやすい
words.say: Before that, I worked as a software engineer.

words.answer: I've been with my current company for eight years.
accept: I have been with my current company for eight years.
I've been with my present company for eight years.
I have been with my present company for eight years.
words.q: 今の会社には8年勤めています。（be with を使って）
words.explain: 継続は現在完了 have been with。be with a company は「勤めている」の自然な言い方。I work for eight years は誤り
words.say: I've been with my current company for eight years.

words.answer: My strength is that I learn quickly.
accept: My strength is that I'm a quick learner.
My strength is that I am a quick learner.
My strength is that I'm a fast learner.
My strength is that I learn fast.
words.q: 私の強みは、覚えが早いことです。
words.explain: My strength is that ＋文。名詞1語（My strength is communication）より、文で具体的に言うと説得力が出る
words.say: My strength is that I learn quickly.

words.answer: I'm good at building relationships with clients.
accept: I am good at building relationships with clients.
I'm good at building relationships with customers.
I am good at building relationships with customers.
words.q: 顧客との関係づくりが得意です。
words.explain: good at ＋動名詞。build a relationship with で「関係を築く」。make relationships とは言わない
words.say: I'm good at building relationships with clients.

words.answer: One area I'm working on is public speaking.
accept: One area I am working on is public speaking.
One thing I'm working on is public speaking.
One area I'm working on is speaking in public.
words.q: 改善に取り組んでいる点の一つは、人前で話すことです。
words.explain: weakness と言い切らず area I'm working on と言うと改善中の姿勢が伝わる。work on＝「取り組む」
words.say: One area I'm working on is public speaking.

words.answer: I tend to take on too much work.
accept: I tend to take on too much.
I have a tendency to take on too much work.
words.q: 私は仕事を抱え込みすぎる傾向があります。
words.explain: tend to ＋原形で「〜しがち」。take on＝仕事を引き受ける。I'm a perfectionist は面接官が嫌う定番なので避ける
words.say: I tend to take on too much work.

words.answer: I've been working on this by asking for feedback.
accept: I have been working on this by asking for feedback.
I've been working on it by asking for feedback.
I have been working on it by asking for feedback.
words.q: この点は、フィードバックを求めることで改善に取り組んできました。（work on を使って）
words.explain: 弱みは改善策とセットで。現在完了進行形で「取り組み続けている」。ask for feedback＝意見を求める
words.say: I've been working on this by asking for feedback.

words.answer: I pay close attention to detail.
accept: I pay close attention to details.
I pay attention to detail.
I pay attention to details.
words.q: 私は細部までよく気を配ります。（pay attention を使って）
words.explain: attention to detail が定番。detail は単数が普通。形容詞なら detail-oriented。I'm careful だけでは弱い
words.say: I pay close attention to detail.

words.answer: I work well under pressure.
accept: I perform well under pressure.
I can work well under pressure.
words.q: 私はプレッシャーの中でも力を発揮できます。
words.explain: under pressure で「プレッシャー下で」。in pressure とは言わない。I'm strong to stress は不自然
words.say: I work well under pressure.

words.answer: My colleagues describe me as reliable.
accept: My colleagues would describe me as reliable.
My coworkers describe me as reliable.
My coworkers would describe me as reliable.
words.ja: 他者評価で強みを言う
words.q: 同僚からは、頼りになると言われます。（describe, reliable を使って）
words.explain: describe A as B。「〜と言われる」を I am said to にすると硬い。第三者の評価として言うと押しつけがましくない
words.say: My colleagues describe me as reliable.

words.answer: Let me give you an example.
accept: Let me give you one example.
Let me give an example.
Let me give one example.
words.q: 一つ、例を挙げさせてください。
words.explain: 強みは必ず例で裏づける。give an example が定番。Let me ＋原形。For example, と続けて話し始める
words.say: Let me give you an example.

words.answer: I'm interested in this position because it matches my skills.
accept: I am interested in this position because it matches my skills.
I'm interested in this role because it matches my skills.
I am interested in this role because it matches my skills.
words.q: この職に興味を持ったのは、自分のスキルに合っているからです。（match を使って）
words.explain: interested in ＋名詞。because 以下は理由を1つに絞る。position は「職・ポスト」で job より丁寧
words.say: I'm interested in this position because it matches my skills.

words.answer: What attracted me to your company is your training program.
accept: What attracted me to your company was your training program.
What attracted me to your company is its training program.
What attracted me to your company was its training program.
words.q: 御社に惹かれたのは、研修制度です。（attract を使って）
words.explain: 疑問詞 what の名詞節を主語に。attract は「惹きつける」なので主語は会社側、私は目的語 me
words.say: What attracted me to your company is your training program.

words.answer: I'm looking for a new challenge.
accept: I am looking for a new challenge.
words.q: 私は新しい挑戦を求めているところです。（look for を使って）
words.explain: 転職理由の定番。challenge は可算なので a を忘れない。I want to challenge は目的語がなく不自然
words.say: I'm looking for a new challenge.

words.answer: I want to grow as a project manager.
accept: I'd like to grow as a project manager.
I would like to grow as a project manager.
I hope to grow as a project manager.
words.q: プロジェクトマネージャーとして成長したいと考えています。
words.explain: grow as ＋役職。「成長する」を grow up にすると「大人になる」の意味。役職には a を付ける
words.say: I want to grow as a project manager.

words.answer: Your mission aligns with my values.
accept: Your mission aligns with my own values.
Your company's mission aligns with my values.
Your mission is aligned with my values.
words.q: 御社のミッションは、私の価値観と一致しています。（align を使って）
words.explain: align with で「一致する」。match も可だが align は面接向けの語。values（価値観）は常に複数形
words.say: Your mission aligns with my values.

words.answer: I believe I can contribute to your team.
accept: I believe that I can contribute to your team.
I believe I could contribute to your team.
I believe I can contribute to the team.
words.q: 御社のチームに貢献できると信じています。
words.explain: contribute to ＋対象。contribute だけで止めない。believe は think より確信が強く面接向き
words.say: I believe I can contribute to your team.

words.answer: There was limited room for growth in my previous role.
accept: There was little room for growth in my previous role.
In my previous role, there was limited room for growth.
In my previous role, there was little room for growth.
words.q: 前職では成長の余地が限られていました。（room, previous role を使って）
words.explain: 前職の不満は会社批判にならない言い方で。room for growth＝成長の余地。there was で客観的に述べる
words.say: There was limited room for growth in my previous role.

words.answer: I'd like to broaden my experience.
accept: I would like to broaden my experience.
I want to broaden my experience.
words.q: 経験の幅を広げたいと思っています。（broaden を使って）
words.explain: broaden ＋名詞で「幅を広げる」。widen my experience は不自然。experience は単数・無冠詞
words.say: I'd like to broaden my experience.

words.answer: I can use my language skills in this role.
accept: I can make use of my language skills in this role.
I could use my language skills in this role.
In this role, I can use my language skills.
words.q: この職では、自分の語学力を活かせます。（use, this role を使って）
words.explain: 「活かす」は use ／ make use of。utilize は硬い。language skills は複数形が自然
words.say: I can use my language skills in this role.

words.answer: I was responsible for managing client accounts.
accept: I was responsible for client account management.
I was responsible for the management of client accounts.
words.q: 顧客アカウントの管理を担当していました。（responsible を使って）
words.explain: responsible for ＋動名詞／名詞。過去の担当は過去形 was。responsible to は「〜に対して責任を負う」で別の意味
words.say: I was responsible for managing client accounts.

words.answer: I led a team of five.
accept: I led a team of five people.
I was leading a team of five.
I led a five-person team.
words.q: 私は5人のチームを率いていました。
words.explain: lead の過去形は led（lead のままにしない）。a team of ＋人数が定番。five members より five people が自然
words.say: I led a team of five.

words.answer: I increased sales by twenty percent.
accept: I increased our sales by twenty percent.
words.q: 私は売上を20パーセント伸ばしました。（increase を使って）
words.explain: 増加幅は by ＋数値、「〜まで」なら to。sales は常に複数形。数字を入れると実績の説得力が出る
words.say: I increased sales by twenty percent.

words.answer: I reduced costs by ten percent.
accept: I reduced our costs by ten percent.
words.q: コストを10パーセント削減しました。（reduce を使って）
words.explain: reduce／cut costs by ＋割合。costs は複数形。cost down は和製英語で通じない
words.say: I reduced costs by ten percent.

words.answer: I launched three new products last year.
accept: Last year, I launched three new products.
words.q: 昨年、3つの新製品を立ち上げました。
words.explain: launch は製品・サービスの立ち上げに使う定番動詞。last year があるので過去形。位置は文末か文頭
words.say: I launched three new products last year.

words.answer: I managed a budget of two million dollars.
accept: I managed a two-million-dollar budget.
I was managing a budget of two million dollars.
words.q: 200万ドルの予算を管理していました。（manage を使って）
words.explain: a budget of ＋金額。「管理」は manage が最も自然（control は監視の響き）。dollars は複数形
words.say: I managed a budget of two million dollars.

words.answer: I worked closely with the marketing team.
accept: I worked closely with the marketing department.
I collaborated closely with the marketing team.
words.q: マーケティングチームと密に連携して働きました。（closely を使って）
words.explain: work closely with で「密に連携する」。cooperate with は少し硬い。特定のチームには the
words.say: I worked closely with the marketing team.

words.answer: In my current role, I oversee daily operations.
accept: In my current position, I oversee daily operations.
In my current job, I oversee daily operations.
In my current role, I oversee the daily operations.
words.q: 現職では、日々の業務を統括しています。（oversee を使って）
words.explain: In my current role, で切り出すと経歴が整理される。oversee は「全体を見る」で manage より上位の響き
words.say: In my current role, I oversee daily operations.

words.answer: We achieved our annual target two months early.
accept: We achieved the annual target two months early.
We achieved our yearly target two months early.
We achieved our annual goal two months early.
words.q: 私たちは年間目標を2か月前倒しで達成しました。（achieve, early を使って）
words.explain: achieve／meet／reach a target。「前倒しで」は early または ahead of schedule。target は単数
words.say: We achieved our annual target two months early.

words.answer: The situation was that we lost a major client.
accept: The situation was that we had lost a major client.
The situation was that we'd lost a major client.
words.q: 状況としては、私たちは大口顧客を失っていました。（major client を使って）
words.explain: STAR 法の S。The situation was that ＋文で話の場面を先に置く。major client＝大口顧客。lose の過去形は lost
words.say: The situation was that we lost a major client.

words.answer: My task was to win them back.
accept: My task was to win the client back.
My task was to win back the client.
My job was to win them back.
words.q: 私の任務は、その顧客を取り戻すことでした。（win back を使って）
words.explain: STAR の T。My task was to ＋原形。win back＝取り戻す。目的語が代名詞なら win them back の語順
words.say: My task was to win them back.

words.answer: First, I met with the client to listen to their concerns.
accept: First, I met with the client to hear their concerns.
First, I met with the client and listened to their concerns.
words.q: まず、顧客と会って懸念を聞きました。（meet with, concerns を使って）
words.explain: STAR の A。First, ／Then, で行動を順に。meet with は仕事上の面談。concerns（懸念点）は複数形が普通
words.say: First, I met with the client to listen to their concerns.

words.answer: As a result, we kept the client.
accept: As a result, we retained the client.
As a result, we were able to keep the client.
As a result, we were able to retain the client.
words.q: その結果、私たちはその顧客を維持できました。
words.explain: STAR の R。As a result, で結果を示す。retain は「引き留める」でビジネス寄り。As the result にしない
words.say: As a result, we kept the client.

words.answer: I learned the importance of clear communication.
accept: I learned how important clear communication is.
I learnt the importance of clear communication.
I learned the importance of communicating clearly.
words.q: 明確なコミュニケーションの大切さを学びました。
words.explain: 話は「学び」で締めると評価される。the importance of ＋名詞。communication は不可算
words.say: I learned the importance of clear communication.

words.answer: We had a disagreement about the schedule.
accept: We had a disagreement over the schedule.
There was a disagreement about the schedule.
There was a disagreement over the schedule.
words.q: スケジュールについて意見の対立がありました。（disagreement を使って）
words.explain: conflict より disagreement の方が穏やか。about／over のどちらも可。fight は喧嘩に聞こえる
words.say: We had a disagreement about the schedule.

words.answer: I suggested a compromise that worked for everyone.
accept: I suggested a compromise that worked for everybody.
I suggested a compromise that would work for everyone.
words.q: 全員が納得できる妥協案を提案しました。（suggest, work for を使って）
words.explain: suggest ＋名詞（suggest to do は誤り）。work for ＋人で「〜にとってうまくいく」。compromise は可算
words.say: I suggested a compromise that worked for everyone.

words.answer: I enjoy working as part of a team.
accept: I enjoy working as a part of a team.
I enjoy working as a member of a team.
I enjoy working in a team.
words.q: チームの一員として働くのが好きです。（enjoy を使って）
words.explain: enjoy ＋動名詞。as part of a team が定番。I like team play は和製英語。具体例を続けると強い
words.say: I enjoy working as part of a team.

words.answer: We had a tight deadline, so I prioritized the key tasks.
accept: We had a tight deadline, so I prioritised the key tasks.
The deadline was tight, so I prioritized the key tasks.
We had a tight deadline, so I prioritized the important tasks.
We had a tight deadline, so I prioritized the most important tasks.
words.q: 締切が厳しかったので、重要なタスクを優先しました。（tight deadline, prioritize を使って）
words.explain: tight deadline＝厳しい締切。prioritize＝優先順位をつける。so で「原因→自分の行動」をつなぐ
words.say: We had a tight deadline, so I prioritized the key tasks.

words.answer: I made a mistake, but I reported it immediately.
accept: I made a mistake but reported it immediately.
I made a mistake, but I reported it right away.
I made a mistake, but I reported it at once.
words.q: ミスをしましたが、すぐに報告しました。
words.explain: 失敗は隠さず「すぐ報告した」で締めると誠実さが伝わる。make a mistake（do a mistake ではない）
words.say: I made a mistake, but I reported it immediately.

words.answer: Could you repeat the question?
accept: Could you repeat the question, please?
Could you please repeat the question?
Would you repeat the question?
words.q: 質問をもう一度言っていただけますか。
words.explain: Could you ＋原形で丁寧に。repeat の後に again は不要（意味が重複）。Pardon? だけでは面接では軽い
words.say: Could you repeat the question?

words.answer: Do you mean my current job or my previous one?
accept: Do you mean my current job or my last one?
Do you mean my current position or my previous one?
Do you mean my current role or my previous one?
words.q: 現職のことでしょうか、それとも前職のことでしょうか。
words.explain: Do you mean ＋名詞で意図を確認する。one は job の繰り返しを避ける代名詞。確認してから答えれば的外れを防げる
words.say: Do you mean my current job or my previous one?

words.answer: That's a good question.
accept: That is a good question.
That's a great question.
words.q: （考える時間を作る一言）それは、いい質問ですね。
words.explain: 考える時間を稼ぐ定番。乱用すると軽く聞こえるので面接中1回まで。難しい質問への前置きにも使える
words.say: That's a good question.

words.answer: Let me think for a moment.
accept: Let me think about that for a moment.
Let me think for a second.
Let me think about it for a moment.
words.q: 少しの間、考えさせてください。
words.explain: 沈黙するより一言添える。Please wait は命令に聞こえる。for a moment を付けると自然で丁寧
words.say: Let me think for a moment.

words.answer: Could you rephrase that, please?
accept: Could you rephrase that?
Could you please rephrase that?
Could you rephrase the question?
words.q: 別の言い方で言っていただけますか。（rephrase を使って）
words.explain: 聞き取れたが意味が分からないときは repeat ではなく rephrase。that は相手の直前の発言を指す
words.say: Could you rephrase that, please?

words.answer: If I understand correctly, you're asking about my goals.
accept: If I understand correctly, you are asking about my goals.
If I understand you correctly, you're asking about my goals.
If I understand you correctly, you are asking about my goals.
words.q: 私の理解が正しければ、私の目標についてのご質問ですね。（ask about を使って）
words.explain: If I understand correctly, で言い換えて確認する。you're asking と進行形にすると「今のご質問は」の意味
words.say: If I understand correctly, you're asking about my goals.

words.answer: May I come back to that later?
accept: Could I come back to that later?
Can I come back to that later?
May I come back to that question later?
words.q: その点は後ほどお答えしてもよろしいですか。（come back to を使って）
words.explain: come back to＝話題に戻る。May I が最も丁寧。思い出せないときに沈黙するより誠実な対応
words.say: May I come back to that later?

words.answer: I'm sorry, I didn't catch that.
accept: Sorry, I didn't catch that.
I'm sorry, I did not catch that.
I am sorry, I didn't catch that.
words.ja: 聞き取れなかったとき
words.q: すみません、聞き取れませんでした。（catch を使って）
words.explain: catch＝聞き取る。I can't hear you は音量の問題に聞こえる。I don't understand は失礼に響くことがある
words.say: I'm sorry, I didn't catch that.

words.answer: What does a typical day look like?
accept: What does a typical day look like in this role?
What is a typical day like?
What would a typical day look like?
words.q: 典型的な1日はどのような感じですか。
words.explain: What does 〜 look like? で「どんな感じか」。How is a typical day? は不自然。in this role を添えると具体的
words.say: What does a typical day look like?

words.answer: What are the next steps?
accept: What are the next steps in the process?
What is the next step?
What's the next step?
words.q: 次のステップはどのようになりますか。
words.explain: 選考の流れを聞く定番。steps は複数形が普通。What's the next schedule? は不自然
words.say: What are the next steps?

words.answer: How do you measure success in this role?
accept: How is success measured in this role?
How do you measure success in this position?
How would you measure success in this role?
words.q: この職では、成功はどのように測られますか。（measure, this role を使って）
words.explain: measure success＝成果を測る。evaluate は人事評価寄り。in this role で範囲を絞ると答えやすい質問になる
words.say: How do you measure success in this role?

words.answer: Could you tell me more about the team?
accept: Could you tell me a bit more about the team?
Can you tell me more about the team?
Could you tell me a little more about the team?
words.q: チームについてもう少し教えていただけますか。
words.explain: tell me more about が定番。teach は「教科を教える」なので使わない。please を付けるなら文末
words.say: Could you tell me more about the team?

words.answer: What are the biggest challenges in this role?
accept: What are the biggest challenges of this role?
What is the biggest challenge in this role?
What's the biggest challenge in this role?
words.q: この職での最大の課題は何ですか。（challenge を使って）
words.explain: challenge は「取り組みがいのある課題」。problem と言うとネガティブに響く。最上級には the
words.say: What are the biggest challenges in this role?

words.answer: Yes, I have a couple of questions.
accept: Yes, I do have a couple of questions.
Yes, I've got a couple of questions.
words.q: はい、2つほど質問があります。（a couple of を使って）
words.explain: 「質問はありますか」に No と答えると意欲が低く見える。a couple of＝2つほど。question は可算
words.say: Yes, I have a couple of questions.

words.answer: What opportunities are there for professional development?
accept: What professional development opportunities are there?
Are there opportunities for professional development?
What opportunities are there for professional growth?
words.q: 能力開発の機会にはどのようなものがありますか。（professional development を使って）
words.explain: professional development＝スキルアップの機会。Can I grow? と聞くと幼い印象。opportunities は複数形
words.say: What opportunities are there for professional development?

words.answer: When can I expect to hear from you?
accept: When can I expect to hear back from you?
When could I expect to hear from you?
When might I expect to hear from you?
words.q: いつごろご連絡をいただけそうでしょうか。（expect を使って）
words.explain: hear from＝連絡をもらう。When will you contact me? は催促に聞こえる。expect を挟むと柔らかい
words.say: When can I expect to hear from you?

words.answer: Thank you for your time today.
accept: Thank you very much for your time today.
Thank you so much for your time today.
Thank you for taking the time today.
words.q: 本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございました。
words.explain: time には your を付ける。Thank you for today だけでは物足りない。最後は笑顔で会釈か握手
words.say: Thank you for your time today.

words.answer: I look forward to hearing from you.
accept: I'm looking forward to hearing from you.
I am looking forward to hearing from you.
words.q: ご連絡をいただけるのを楽しみにしております。
words.explain: look forward to ＋動名詞（to hear は誤り）。面接の締めやお礼メールの定番。現在形の方がやや丁寧
words.say: I look forward to hearing from you.

words.answer: I'm available to start next month.
accept: I am available to start next month.
I can start next month.
I could start next month.
I'd be available to start next month.
words.q: 来月から勤務を開始することが可能です。
words.explain: available to start が定番。「〜から」を from next month としなくてよい。I can start も可
words.say: I'm available to start next month.

words.answer: I need to give one month's notice.
accept: I have to give one month's notice.
I need to give a month's notice.
I'd need to give one month's notice.
words.q: 1か月前に退職を申し出る必要があります。（notice を使って）
words.explain: give notice＝退職を申し出る。one month's notice の所有格 's を忘れやすい。notice は無冠詞
words.say: I need to give one month's notice.

words.answer: My salary expectation is around six million yen.
accept: My expected salary is around six million yen.
My salary expectation is about six million yen.
My expected salary is about six million yen.
My desired salary is around six million yen.
words.q: 希望年収は600万円前後です。
words.explain: salary expectation／expected salary。「前後」は around／about。yen は複数でも yen のまま
words.say: My salary expectation is around six million yen.

words.answer: I'm open to discussing salary.
accept: I am open to discussing salary.
I'm open to discussing the salary.
I am open to discussing the salary.
words.q: 給与については相談に応じます。（open to を使って）
words.explain: open to ＋動名詞／名詞（to discuss は誤り）。discuss は他動詞なので discuss about としない
words.say: I'm open to discussing salary.

words.answer: I'm willing to relocate.
accept: I am willing to relocate.
words.q: 私は転勤にも応じるつもりです。（willing to を使って）
words.explain: willing to＝その気がある。relocate は自動詞で「転居する」。transfer は会社が異動させる側の語
words.say: I'm willing to relocate.

words.answer: It was a pleasure meeting you.
accept: It was a pleasure to meet you.
It's been a pleasure meeting you.
words.q: お会いできてうれしかったです。（pleasure を使って）
words.explain: 別れ際は過去形 was。Nice to meet you は初対面の挨拶なので、去るときは meeting you／was の形
words.say: It was a pleasure meeting you.
